newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Moslem leader undergoes medical treatment.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Moslem leader undergoes medical treatment.

text.p: The Moslem chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, entered a Sarajevo hospital on Thursday for five days of medical treatment, his aide said.

Izetbegovic, 71, who suffered heart trouble last February, went to Kosevo hospital's heart clinic as part of scheduled treatment and his life was not in danger, his spokesman Mirza Hajric told Reuters.
"This was something which was agreed with the doctors for some time," Hajric said.

Izetbegovic was entering hospital at a pivotal moment in discussions over the disputed northern town of Brcko, which is the subject of deep disagreement between the Moslem-Croat federation and the country's Serb republic.

Arbitration hearings in Rome over Brcko were due to finish on Thursday. The arbitration panel, chaired by an American lawyer, must deliver a decision on the future legal status of Brcko by a February 15 deadline.
Doctors wanted to check on Izetbegovic's condition nearly a year after he suffered a heart attack while he was serving as Bosnian president, he said.
Izetbegovic spent some three weeks in hospital last year and later received treatment at home.
Hajric said Izetbegovic would continue to perform his presidential duties during the five-day hospital stay.
"I expect to be in daily touch with him."
Izetbegovic would appoint deputies to represent him at any meetings which he was unable to attend over the next five days, he added.

After leading the country through a 3-1/2 year war of independence against separatist Serb forces, Izetbegovic was elected in September as the Moslem member of a three-man presidency ruling over Serb and Moslem-Croat territories.
Although Izetbegovic is chairman of the collective body, the presidency -- which includes a Serb and Croat members -- must rule by consensus under the terms of a peace agreement.
